Headnote

Contract-law consequences of bribery of a public official.
Contracts procured through kickbacks do not as such have an unlawful or immoral content (confirmation of the case law). A contract procured through bribery of a public official falls under the prohibitory provisions of Art. 19 and 20 OR only if the criminal conduct extends to the content of the contract (E. 5.2).
Formation of the contract despite corruption (E. 6.2)? Non-binding nature of the contract owing to intentional deception (E. 6.3)?
Consequences of avoidance of the contract for defect of consent.
Principle: lapse of the contract ex tunc (E. 7.1.1). In the case of continuing obligations that have been fully or partially performed: termination ex nunc (E. 7.1.2); reservation (E. 7.1.4). Difference from the de facto contractual relationship (E. 7.1.3). Remuneration for services rendered (E. 7.2) and damages (E. 7.3).

Extract from the Federal Act on the Swiss Federal Institutes of Technology (ETH Act) of 4 October 1991 (SR 414.110):

Art. 37 Legal protection
1 The appeal proceedings are governed by the general provisions on the federal administration of justice, unless this Act provides otherwise.
2 The ETH Board, the ETH and the research institutes are entitled to lodge an appeal against appeal decisions if they issued a first-instance ruling in the same matter. The university assemblies are entitled to appeal against rulings on matters of participation.
3 An appeal against rulings of the ETH and the research institutes may be lodged with the ETH Appeal Commission. Excepted are rulings based on the Liability Act of 14 March 1958.
4 In an appeal against rulings on the results of examinations and doctoral procedures, inappropriateness may not be invoked.

Art. 37a ETH Appeal Commission
1 The ETH Board elects the seven members of the ETH Appeal Commission. At least four members must belong to the ETH Domain.
2 The term of office is four years in each case; re-election is possible.
3 The members are independent in their activities and subject only to the law.
4 The Commission is attached to the ETH Board for administrative purposes. It has its own secretariat.
5 The ETH Board issues the rules of procedure. It regulates therein in particular the President’s competence in urgent cases and in cases of minor importance, as well as the formation of chambers with independent decision-making authority.

train_0209:
Yes. Assuming EU law applies (e.g., because the UK was an EU member state at the time, making the London Stock Exchange an EU-regulated market), Hannay violated the EU Market Abuse Regulation (MAR). He possessed inside information within the meaning of Art. 7 MAR: the merger negotiations were precise, non-public, and price-sensitive. His email to Bertie constituted an unlawful disclosure of inside information under Art. 10(1) MAR, which prohibits disclosing inside information to another person except in the normal exercise of one’s employment or profession. A “favour for a friend” is not a permitted disclosure. Art. 14 MAR prohibits both insider dealing and unlawful disclosure. Bertie’s decision not to trade is irrelevant to Hannay’s disclosure offence; the offence was complete upon disclosure. Bertie himself did not engage in insider dealing because he did not acquire or dispose of financial instruments, though he was a tippee.

Under Swiss law, the same conduct violates Art. 142 of the Financial Market Infrastructure Act (FinfraG/FMIA) and Art. 161 of the Swiss Criminal Code (StGB). Art. 142 FMIA prohibits any person who possesses inside information from communicating it to another. Art. 161 StGB criminalises insider trading, including passing on inside information. Hannay had access to inside information through his professional activity as a corporate banker. The fact that the merger was later cancelled and never disclosed does not negate the violation: at the time of disclosure, the information was inside information. The cancellation itself may also have constituted inside information. Bertie, having not traded, did not commit insider dealing, but he received inside information.

Conclusion: Yes, Hannay violated EU MAR (if applicable) and Swiss law. Bertie did not violate insider dealing prohibitions by not trading, but the disclosure itself is a regulatory and criminal offence.

train_0291:
For a bachelor examination in intellectual property law, the title and a few statements from an article in a major daily newspaper are reproduced.

Fashion, an invaluable and unprotectable art

With fashionable clothing it is like with love: it is fleeting, expensive, and in retrospect one must admit to many a faux pas. However, only advanced emotionally impoverished individuals will dispute that love is an art. Little is known about the general position of lawyers on love; on fashion, by contrast, they agree: in the eyes of lawyers, fashion is never art, but a mere utilitarian object. Therefore, fashion cannot in principle be protected under intellectual property law. In addition, even the smallest changes compared with the original suffice, and one can then safely copy the respective fashion item without getting into legal difficulties.

Beneath it, the source (and in particular Anna Alphabet as author) was indicated in parentheses.

The responsible professor writes beneath this original statement:
“Show which statement(s) is/are not correct with regard to Swiss copyright law, justify your answer(s) and explain the actual legal situation.”

Some months later, the professor publishes the examination as an exercise for students on his website. While searching online for her own article, Anna Alphabet comes across this examination. When the estate proceedings in Zurich had been opened, however, she had been completely thunderstruck. Apparently her mother had established a foundation in Liechtenstein in 2015, the Top-Stiftung (TS), and had transferred approximately 90% of her assets to it. The beneficiaries were all her ex-husbands, such as an Italian racing driver, a US singer, an indebted art dealer, a bodyguard, and now also an unemployed former German teen star. Only she, her only daughter, was not a beneficiary of the foundation.

In the proceedings, the question had now arisen whether these assets really belonged to the foundation or whether they must nevertheless be counted as part of the estate. And indeed, investigations had shown that Heidi had exercised considerable influence over the foundation. As the sole first beneficiary during her lifetime, she had reserved an unrestricted right of revocation and amendment; in addition, she had had a mandate agreement with the foundation board that had equipped her with an all-encompassing right to issue instructions: money on demand, as if it had been her bank account. In substance, it was a pure maintenance foundation; there were no conditions for distributions to the beneficiaries. Surely all of this was gross abuse and could not be recognized in Swiss estate proceedings, isn’t that right?

Leni therefore asks you — in a legal opinion — to examine whether the foundation assets should be counted as part of the estate and whether she, as the sole daughter, can access them. Proceed.

114 II 131

22. Judgment of the First Civil Division of 7 June 1988 in the matter of A. v. Mrs X. (appeal)

Headnote

Fundamental mistake of the buyer. Limitation.
1. Art. 23 ff. and 197 ff. OR. In the case of false information or assurances concerning the object of purchase, the buyer may in principle either bring an action for warranty or contest the contract on the ground of a defect in consent (E. 1; confirmation of the case law).
2. Art. 24 Abs. 1 Ziff. 4 OR. Circumstances under which a mistake as to the authenticity of a work of art is to be regarded as essential (E. 2a).
3. Art. 31 OR provides neither expressly nor by implication that the person in error must observe, in addition to the relative period of one year, an absolute period of ten years (E. 2b).
4. Art. 67 Abs. 1 OR. If, after payment of the purchase price, the contract is successfully contested by the buyer on grounds of mistake, the seller's unjust enrichment is to be seen in the payment of a debt not owed. The absolute limitation period for the buyer's claim for restitution therefore begins to run upon payment of the price (E. 3).

In Cameroon, homosexual acts are criminal offences. In the event of violations, penalties may be imposed, at minimum fines and at maximum prison sentences of up to 5 years. Although, according to the wording, only acts are prohibited, persons are arbitrarily placed in pre-trial detention without charge solely on the basis of their actual or presumed homosexual orientation. The statutory offence is applied expansively by the authorities. Arrests and convictions are numerous and have steadily increased in recent years. According to human rights organisations, inhuman, even life-threatening conditions prevail in prisons. Apart from constant overcrowding and inadequate hygiene, torture is even widespread in order to induce the accused to make statements. Furthermore, detainees accused of homosexuality are frequently victims of discrimination, verbal and physical violence, and rape by other prison inmates or by staff. Cameroonian society is called upon by politicians and priests to report homosexuals and to “hunt” them. The climate in the country is homophobic; same-sex love is regarded as a great shame. Homosexuals are therefore often humiliated and abused within their families as well.

The Cameroonian national Kiano is homosexual. He had already secretly had various same-sex romantic relationships. He was already imprisoned three times for this reason and, as he reports, tortured. The last time was in 2016. After that, he went into hiding and stayed hidden from authorities, families and friends, as he could no longer endure the burdensome situation. The outline is said to be in the attachment. The professor opens the Word document, which indeed contains a rudimentary outline on a seminar topic, whereby his computer is infected with the software. Hosting

§ 3 VbVG – Liability
(1) An association* is, under the further conditions of Abs. 2 or Abs. 3, liable for a criminal offence if
1. the offence was committed for its benefit, or
2. duties incumbent on the association were violated by the offence.
(2) The association is liable for criminal offences of a decision-maker if the decision-maker as such committed the offence unlawfully and culpably.
(3) The association is liable for criminal offences of staff members if
1. staff members unlawfully realized the facts corresponding to the statutory offence description; the association is liable for a criminal offence requiring intentional conduct only if a staff member acted intentionally; for a criminal offence requiring negligent conduct, only if staff members failed to exercise the care required under the circumstances; and
2. the commission of the offence was made possible or substantially facilitated by decision-makers failing to exercise the care required and reasonable under the circumstances, in particular by omitting essential technical, organisational or personnel measures to prevent such offences.
(a) The liability of an association for an offence and the criminal liability of decision-makers or staff members for the same offence do not exclude one another.
* The term  is identical to the term  in Art.I02 StGB.

Mandate or extra-contractual conduct? Capacity to be sued.

In Cameroon, homosexual acts constitute criminal offences. Violations can be punished by fines at a minimum and by prison sentences of up to 5 years at a maximum. Although, according to the wording, only acts are prohibited, persons are arbitrarily placed in pre-trial detention without charge solely on the basis of their actual or presumed homosexual orientation. The offence is applied expansively by the authorities. Arrests and convictions are numerous and have steadily increased in recent years. According to human rights organisations, conditions in prisons are inhuman, even life-threatening. Apart from constant overcrowding and lack of hygiene, torture is even widespread in order to induce the accused to make statements. Furthermore, detainees accused of homosexuality are frequently victims of discrimination, verbal and physical violence and rape by other prison inmates or by staff. Cameroonian society is called upon by politicians and priests to report homosexuals and to “hunt” them. The climate in the country is homophobic; same-sex love is regarded as a great shame. Homosexuals are therefore often also humiliated and abused within their families.

The Cameroonian national Kiano is homosexual. He has secretly had various same-sex love relationships. He has already been imprisoned three times for this reason and, as he reports, tortured. The last time was in 2016. Afterwards he went into hiding and stayed hidden from authorities, family and friends, since he could no longer endure the distressing situation. Thanks to a brief search, he was able to establish that his sculpture is being used one-to-one in various ways in the watch group’s new advertising campaign. On the one hand, famous actors and actresses are posing next to a faithful reproduction of the astronaut sculpture at the Venice International Film Festival. On the other hand, the astronaut appears on posters for the new watch collection that have been put up in cities all over the world. Xavier is both furious and discouraged: he feels powerless against the large luxury group. Nevertheless, he decides to discuss this case with his friends who are studying law. 
Assume that the sculpture deserves legal protection under this law. Which rights of Xavier could have been infringed by the watch group through the unauthorized use of his sculpture in advertising and its subtle alteration (reduction in size, change of color from silver to gold)? Can the watch group invoke grounds of justification? If so, which ones?

It wishes to increase the minimum cost-sharing (retention and deductible) from today's 1'000 Franken to 5'000 Franken per insured person and to enshrine this in Art. 64 KVG. train_0804:
Jet boats on Lake Lucerne
Facts Part I
In December 2015, on the basis of a newspaper report, the environmental association Pro Natura became aware that jet boats would be available on Lake Lucerne near Weggis, Canton of Lucerne, from spring 2016 as a new leisure activity. These were to be operated by the Municipality of Weggis to promote tourism. In the territory of the Municipality of Weggis there are several hotels important for tourism. The municipality wishes to offer its guests something.
Pro Natura subsequently wrote a letter in early 2016 to the Lake Police of the Canton of Lucerne, requesting that it be served without delay “an appealable ruling granting the permit for increased common use, for passenger transport and, if applicable, further permits (fishing, water protection, etc.)”.
The Lake Police replied to the letter as early as 22 January 2016 to the effect that the jet boats were not subject to a permit requirement if they complied with the exhaust and noise regulations, which was the case. Therefore, there were no permits that could be served.
Pro Natura then promptly challenged this “with kind regards” letter, i.e. already on 29 January 2016, within the time limit before the competent cantonal appellate authority. By decision of 26 February 2016, the latter did not enter into the appeal for lack of a sufficient subject matter of appeal.
Preliminary note: Answer the question posed, to the extent relevant, on the basis of the VwVG and not cantonal law.
Can Pro Natura already lodge an appeal in the cantonal proceedings? (Examine all requirements, even if you deny one of the requirements for lodging an appeal).

Nico is 17 years old. He grew up in Bazenheid in problematic family circumstances. His father was an alcoholic and often let his fists do the talking when raising him. When Nico was in the third grade, his father went out one Saturday morning “to buy cigarettes” and never returned. Thereupon his mother began to drown her pain in alcohol. Today Nico sees his mother only occasionally. Although he is officially still registered at his mother’s, he lives almost entirely with his grandparents in Winterthur. Nico came to the attention of the criminal authorities at an early age, committed several thefts, and often got into brawls with his classmates. He is the leader of his gang “WW” (Westside Winterthur). His rank in the gang is secure. No one would dare to question Nico’s position, since he beat those who tried until they needed hospital treatment. It has also happened that Nico beat up someone who looked at him “the wrong way.” Nico knows that his actions are not right, but he does not care. Overall, Nico appears to have a deep anger toward his fellow human beings and the world. Only with his plants does he always act very lovingly. He spends a lot of money on cultivating his rare specimens. He decides that he could obtain this most easily through armed robberies of gas stations. However, he is caught on the very first robbery.
Who is the competent investigating authority in the present case?

They come to Notary Caduff, who works at a notary's office in Kanton Zürich and is known for his conscientiousness and diligence. The two present him with a printout of a written power of attorney in which Anna authorizes her husband Beat to represent her before the Kenyan notary and the Kenyan authorities, including signing the purchase contract. They ask Notary Caduff to certify the authenticity of Anna's signature on the document by notarial act and to obtain the additional official certification necessary for use of the power of attorney in Kenia. Notary Caduff does this with all due care. In the meantime, the notary's office has introduced the full technical infrastructure for producing electronic versions of public deeds. At Beat's request, Notary Caduff now creates a scan of the entire written power of attorney, including his notarial electronic certification that the scan conforms to the paper document. However, due to an oversight during scanning, the bottom two lines are missing on the first page of the electronic version. Immediately after delivery of the electronic version, the Kenyan notary notices the error in the electronic document and draws Beat's attention to it. Beat is furious and files a complaint against Notary Caduff with the competent supervisory authority; the latter deeply regrets the oversight. On the occasion of Lisa's birth, Sameer and Tina agreed that Tina would personally care for Lisa at least until she started primary school. Afterwards, she moved with Lisa to Sameer's condominium in Zurich. Sameer runs a small accounting firm on a self-employed basis. His parents are of the Buddhist faith and come from India. Sameer himself, however, has spent his entire life in Switzerland.
Sameer has a son named Leo (born 1.1.1993) from a previous relationship. Due to his gap year (a year between Matura and university), his economics studies abandoned after one semester, and occasionally failed exams, he has only now begun his master's degree in medicine. He lives in a shared apartment with two friends. Leo has had no contact with his mother for a long time.
For half a year, the relationship between Sameer and Tina has no longer been running smoothly. Tina is generally dissatisfied. Sameer is mainly troubled by the fact that Leo is becoming increasingly distant from him. Leo has never liked Tina. Since Lisa's birth, he feels increasingly neglected because, in his opinion, his father has focused too much on his new family over the past year. The KKL, situated directly on Lake Lucerne, is known throughout Europe in particular for its 9'400 m2 flat roof, which projects far beyond the building and is larger than a football pitch.

He sends the software hidden in a Word document (“Disposition.docx”) by email to the professor. In the email, he asks the professor to supervise his seminar paper. The outline was said to be in the attachment. The professor opens the Word document, which in fact contained a rudimentary outline on a seminar topic, as a result of which his computer became infected with the software. In the following night, on 8 February at 2:00 a.m., Thomas accesses the professor's computer, searches for the file containing the grades (which had already been recorded), and changes his grade 3 to a grade 5.5. When the professor comes into his office the next morning, he sees that his computer is running.
Thomas had forgotten to shut it down again using his software. Because this seemed suspicious to him, he examines his files closely. In doing so, he sees that the file containing the grades was last saved at 2:10 a.m. After consulting with his team, he decides to file a criminal complaint with the police.

Shortly thereafter, the art dealer offered the painting for sale in her gallery. As a result, both the Swiss art collector and the Italian Ministry of Culture became aware of the painting. In Cameroon, homosexual acts are criminal offences. In the case of violations, fines at a minimum and prison sentences of up to 5 years at a maximum may be imposed. Although, according to the wording, only acts are prohibited, persons are arbitrarily placed in pre-trial detention without charge solely on the basis of their actual or presumed homosexual orientation. The offence is applied expansively by the authorities. Arrests and convictions are numerous and have steadily increased in recent years. According to human rights organizations, inhuman, even life-threatening conditions prevail in the prisons. Apart from constant overcrowding and poor hygiene, torture is even widespread in order to induce the accused to make statements. Furthermore, detainees accused of homosexuality are frequently victims of discrimination, verbal and physical violence, and rape by other prison inmates or by staff. Cameroonian society is called upon by politicians and priests to report homosexuals and to “hunt” them. The climate in the country is homophobic; same-sex love is regarded as a great shame. Homosexuals are therefore often humiliated and mistreated within their families as well.

The Cameroonian national Kiano is homosexual. He has already secretly had various same-sex love relationships. He has already been imprisoned three times for that reason and, as he reports, tortured. The last time was in 2016. Afterwards he went into hiding and remained hidden from authorities, families and friends, because he could no longer endure the burdensome situation.
